speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the root cause, can you describe exactly what these unusual physical features look like?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned a history of bone fragility; can you specify if you have experienced any fractures from minor trauma, and have any imaging been done to assess bone density? Also, do you have any family members with a similar history of delayed puberty or unusual physical features?

speaker: Doctor
text: The bone density and karyotype results are pending, but your history of partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly, and maternal hirsutism strongly suggests a congenital adrenal hyperplasia variant. Have you ever been tested for 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels or androgen levels? Also, do you have any other symptoms like deepening of the voice or excessive muscle mass?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (likely 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency). The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, maternal hirsutism during pregnancy, and virilizing features like severe acne and clitoromegaly is classic for this condition, which also explains the delayed menarche due to hormonal imbalance affecting the HPO axis.
